name: managed USDC quote asset fails closed, then reaches high-risk review
description: A v4 pool using an issuer-controlled quote asset must resolve issuer, legal, router and unwind facts and integrate the mandatory Programmable volume fee. It is not Uniswap's official permissioned-pool architecture and makes no issuer, routing or availability approval claim.

model.name: Managed USDC Quote Launch
model.summary: Launch one USDC-quoted canonical pool while making the quote asset's issuer controls and unwind limits explicit.
model.userOutcome: A participant can trade the launched token against USDC with visible issuer, routing and unwind dependencies.
model.whyV4: An afterSwap hook records canonical-pool activity without changing core settlement or pretending to override USDC issuer controls.

controls: Issuer may block addresses under the USDC terms

pool.orderingRule: Mine the launched-token CREATE2 salt so its predicted address sorts after the documented USDC address; otherwise regenerate the PoolKey before implementation.

callbackPolicies.necessity: The hook records one pool-scoped aggregate only after a completed USDC swap.
callbackPolicies.allowedReverts: Only invalid PoolId admission or an atomic storage failure may revert the complete action.
callbackPolicies.userExitImpact: This callback does not govern swaps, claims or liquidity removal.
callbackPolicies.noSelfCallImpact: The model initiates no nested PoolManager or router action.

authorities.controller: Circle-administered roles at the declared Ethereum USDC contract
authorities.userExitImpact: Issuer action can make a USDC swap or liquidity removal fail even when the hook remains available.

permissionedAsset.jurisdiction: USDC issuer terms and each participant's applicable law govern eligibility; the pool makes no universal jurisdiction claim.
permissionedAsset.underlyingClaim: USDC redemption rights remain subject to Circle terms and account eligibility; pairing does not create a claim on the launched token.
permissionedAsset.custodian: USDC reserve and redemption arrangements remain Circle dependencies and are never represented as Programmable custody.
permissionedAsset.hooks: The immutable v4 hook records aggregate activity and never overrides USDC transfer controls.
permissionedAsset.positionManager: The standard v4 PositionManager remains authoritative; this proposal adds no privileged position-transfer path.
permissionedAsset.swapEligibility: The hook adds no allowlist; USDC transfers remain subject to issuer controls, account status, terms and applicable law.
permissionedAsset.liquidityEligibility: The hook adds no liquidity allowlist; USDC transfer controls can still make addition or removal fail.
permissionedAsset.positionTransferability: The hook adds no position restriction and does not claim that transfer changes USDC terms or issuer controls.
permissionedAsset.redemption: USDC redemption is exclusively subject to Circle terms; the launched token has no issuer redemption promise.

operations.monitoring: Alert on USDC transfer failures, issuer-control events and changes to the declared USDC implementation.
operations.incidentResponse: Stop presenting new routes when issuer or runtime checks fail; preserve all hook-layer exit paths and disclose issuer limits.

rationales.complexity: Issuer controls, router binding and a two-asset failure matrix expand the standard launch path.
rationales.customMath: The hook uses no custom price curve, fee formula or return-delta arithmetic.
rationales.externalDependencies: Trading depends on USDC issuer controls and one exact router generation.
rationales.externalLiquidity: The hook holds no external inventory, vault share, PoolManager claim or beneficiary balance.
rationales.valueAtRisk: Issuer controls or transfer failure can interrupt a pool containing user and LP value.
rationales.teamMaturity: A conservative nonzero process score remains until legal and security reviews are complete.
rationales.upgradeability: The quote token is an upgradeable issuer dependency even though the hook and launched token are immutable.
rationales.autonomy: No keeper, oracle or autonomous parameter can alter pool behavior.
rationales.priceImpact: The observer does not change core price math, LP fees or settlement deltas.

disclosures: This is a standard v4 pool with a managed quote asset, not Uniswap's Permissions Adapter, PermissionedHooks and Permissioned Position Manager architecture.
This proposal is not issuer approval, legal approval, routing approval or evidence that the pool is available.
Circle does not provide or endorse this pool; Circle remains only the external USDC issuer dependency.
USDC pause, blacklist or upgrade behavior can interrupt swaps and may also prevent an otherwise standard unwind.

onchain.name: Uniswap Universal Router 2.2
onchain.trust: The proposal pairs an exact source candidate with the committed deployment record; a prototype must prove source and runtime identity before execution.
onchain.failure: A missing or mismatched router record blocks route preparation before any transaction is produced.
onchain.fallback: No silent router fallback is allowed; select and review another exact generation.

permissionedAsset.issuer: Circle Internet Financial or the applicable Circle USDC issuer under the linked USDC terms.
permissionedAsset.adapter: No currency adapter is used: the PoolKey contains the documented Ethereum USDC contract and the hook adds no eligibility layer.
permissionedAsset.pauseFreezeUnwind: On USDC pause, blocklist or transfer failure, new routes fail closed. The hook never blocks removal, but it cannot promise completion when USDC itself rejects transfer; no rescue path bypasses issuer controls.
permissionedAsset.routingLimitations: Only the exact Universal Router 2.2 record is encoded. Quotes and transactions surface issuer controls, final-delta bounds and USDC transfer failure; no routing provider approval is claimed.

dependencyFailure.actor: A trader or liquidity provider encounters a USDC or router dependency failure.
dependencyFailure.valueFlow: The complete action reverts before partial settlement and no hook balance is created.
dependencyFailure.custody: The hook never receives USDC or launched tokens during a failed dependency call.
dependencyFailure.failure: New routes fail closed; removal remains ungated by the hook but still depends on USDC transfer liveness.
dependencyFailure.event: The application records the failed dependency class offchain without claiming an onchain lifecycle transition.

retirement.actor: The application stops offering new routes when issuer terms, controls or runtime identity assumptions change.
retirement.valueFlow: Existing positions keep the standard PoolManager removal path; no migration or redemption is promised.
retirement.custody: Neither the hook nor application takes custody during retirement.
retirement.failure: USDC issuer controls may still prevent transfer, and the interface must disclose that external limitation.
retirement.event: A versioned registry status marks the model retired for new launches without claiming the pool is closed.
